answer: Correlation penalties: when many accounts behave like one river splitting into channels (same timing, phrasing, funding source), the ledger shrinks every account's reward by how closely it tracks its siblings. A sybil farm carved like a canyon by one hand earns about what a single agent would, yet still pays registration and compute for each fake. Honest agents on an independent voyage diverge naturally and keep full rewards, so splitting identities stops being profitable.
